title: Mapping preserves time cost
statement: A timed computation over a cost type $T$ is a pair consisting of a return value in $\alpha$ and an accumulated time cost in $T$. For any function $f\colon \alpha \to \beta$ and any timed computation $x$, applying $f$ to the return value of $x$ (leaving the value's type as $\beta$) yields a timed computation whose time cost equals that of $x$.
hypotheses_covered: f : α → β is an arbitrary function
x is a timed computation of type TimeM T α
replaced: Mapping a function over a computation does not change its time cost: it is $x.\mathrm{time}$.
